impacted.role: The get_feedback_statistics method counts topics_upvoted and topics_downvoted from each voted item's matched_interests and builds for_llm_context from the top five of each list; this is where a vote becomes a liked or disliked topic.
get_learned_preferences is the one fetch of for_llm_context for the evaluator, gated only on min_votes=5 total; all three evaluator callers go through it.

ContextAutoUpdater feeds the raw topics_upvoted and topics_downvoted lists to an LLM told to demote downvoted topics and writes its output over context.md; check_context_md already parses context.md into its ## sections.
Appends the learned-preferences string to the system prompt as flat 'User prefers' / 'User dislikes' statements under a prose 'SUPPLEMENT (not override)' line.
run_once fetches learned preferences once per cycle and threads them to every item's evaluation; it holds self.config.context.
run_refetch fetches learned preferences the same way for re-analysed items, and carries the dry-run cost estimate a re-score can reuse.
The repair command fetches learned preferences through the same helper and already builds a Config.
Existing tests of get_feedback_statistics' dict shape and time filter; the new evidence and context-precedence tests sit beside them.

constraints.text: topics_downvoted is counted in its own loop, separate from topics_upvoted at line 2530, with no comparison between the two counts for one topic.
Any topic with one downvote enters the top-five 'User dislikes' list, and a topic can sit in both 'User prefers' and 'User dislikes' in the same string.
The only evidence bar is total_votes < min_votes (5) across all topics; after that, no per-topic count is required.
Learned preferences are told to 'SUPPLEMENT (not override)' the context in prose only; nothing in code limits what they say.

Measured 2026-10-15 (issue #96 comment): re-evaluating 100 items since 2026-10-08 gave 80% null live, 30% with only the 'User dislikes' part removed, 35% with no learned preferences, 71% with the pre-b6c3f70 prompt and 75% with the pre-Agentic context.
The dislike list is the cause of the drop, and the liked list is not harmful: likes without dislikes scored slightly better than no learned preferences.
<host> has 25 votes in total (24 up, 1 down); the single downvote's three matched_interests are all High-section bullets that also carry 10 to 11 upvotes each.
Real vote data cannot calibrate a minimum downvote count: there is one downvote to learn from.

Of 7,344 matched_interests labels since 2026-08-15, 3,745 are exact context bullets, 3,266 are ### group headings (252 of them differing only in case), 248 are bullets without their parenthetical, 33 are bullet fragments or prefixes, and 52 match no context line.

A label resolves to its context line, and so to its ## section, for 99.3% of labels when matched case-insensitively, with parentheticals and extra spaces dropped, against both bullets and ### headings, falling back to bullet prefix or fragment.
A learned dislike can never name a topic from the context's High or Medium sections, enforced in code.

A label that resolves to no context line cannot be shown to sit outside High and Medium, so emitting it as a dislike could break the rule; the rule holds only if an unresolved label is never emitted as a dislike.
The auto-updater prompt says 'Downvoted topics: Demote (HIGH→MED, MED→LOW→Not Interested)', and its topic lists come straight from get_feedback_statistics at line 257.
The LLM's output is written over context.md after a validation that checks only that the three required headings, a '- ' bullet and no code fence are present; nothing checks which topics moved.

auto_update_enabled defaults to True, so every user gets the auto-updater unless they turn it off; <host> has it on, last ran 2026-09-26T05:42Z (only added --- wrappers) and is next due about 2026-10-26.

A fix confined to for_llm_context leaves the auto-updater able to demote a High topic on the same one downvote, which breaks the decided rule that explicit context outranks learned preferences, through a rewrite of the context itself.
The feedback loop's stated vision is that votes evolve context.md automatically with no manual editing, so the auto-updater is intended behavior to make safe, not a stray feature.
A trigger sets content.updated_at on every update to a row, and the content table has no column recording when a vote was cast.

The since_days window filters votes on c.updated_at; on <host> every voted row from 2026-09-30 shares updated_at 21:40:16Z from one bulk write, while the downvote was cast 2026-09-29T20:03:59Z per the obs log.
Keying the window on vote time needs a new column and a migration through _MIGRATIONS in database.py, with no exact vote time for existing votes.
GET /api/feedback/statistics returns get_feedback_statistics' dict unchanged, including the raw topic lists and for_llm_context.

Every evaluator caller (orchestrator line 588, refetch.py line 338, cli analyze.py line 133) gets learned preferences through get_learned_preferences and has a Config in scope, so the context's sections are available where the gate runs.
run_refetch's dry run multiplies upper_bound_cost_estimate by the selected count; no command re-scores already-readable items, and b6c3f70's re-score of 841 items was an ad hoc script.

Evaluate calls cost a median $0.00063 and p99 $0.0043 on <host>; the OpenRouter account had about $1.02 of $150 credit left on 2026-10-15 and returned 402 in_flight_budget_exhausted under 8 parallel calls.

related.query: gh issue list --state all --search "feedback OR preference OR context.md OR vote" --limit 20

issues.why: Sibling split from this work: detects an unprioritized-share jump; its done-when replays the Sep 30 step this fix removes.
Closed vote-integrity bug (a PATCH without user_feedback cleared votes); the vote write path it fixed is the input this work reads.
Multi-context profiles would give each profile its own High/Medium sections; the context-precedence gate should take the context as an argument rather than read one global file.

reuse.what: check_context_md's line walk that assigns each bullet to its ## section, treating ### groups as part of the section above, for resolving labels to sections.
get_learned_preferences as the single gate every evaluator caller already goes through.
run_refetch's dry-run and per-item outcome pattern, and upper_bound_cost_estimate, for the re-score.
Its test_db fixture and seeding of voted content for the new evidence and precedence tests.
